messages.author: 631012ad99806a53
messages.subject: scale_x_datetime question
parts:
Dear ggplot2 users,

I am dealing with data of hourly values, taken over a certain number of months. What I want to do is a frequency histogram that shows the percentage of occurrences at certain hours within the day. The data frame was pre-filtered, so everything needed for the plot should be the timestamps in POSIXct format. Dummy data looks something like:

m <- data.frame(date = as.POSIXct(seq(1, 1000, 1)*3600, origin = "2004-01-01 00:00:00"))

I have gotten as far as:

ggplot(m, aes(x=format(m$date, "%H:%M:%S"))) + geom_histogram(aes(y = ..count../sum(..count..))) + scale_y_continuous(formatter="percent")

I am trying to scale the x axis to a readable format, say tics at every 3 hours. I found scale_x_datetime, but it is used for continuous scales as I understood. Is there a better way than the format function?

Any ides or pointers? Thanks in advance

Michael Bach

messages.author: 9e8f9b870a2e6cdf
messages.subject: Re: scale_x_datetime question
parts:
How about:

m$hour <- as.POSIXlt(m$date)$hour
ggplot(m,aes(x=hour))+geom_histogram(aes(y = ..count../sum(..count..)),binwidth=1)+scale_y_continuous(formatter="percent")

Have fun,
Frans.

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: scale_x_datetime question
parts:
Hi:

Assuming you want to aggregate over days, one approach would be to generate a data frame with hour as one of the variables. You could use the cut() function to produce subintervals of hours as factor levels and use its labels = argument to set the labels. As long as the labels are ordered, you should then be able to get the histogram directly, although if you were to follow this suggestion, geom_bar() would likely be more appropriate since cut() produces a factor rather than a numeric variable.

HTH,
Dennis

ggplot(m, aes(x=as.POSIXct(format(m$date, "2000/01/01 %H:%M:%S")))) +
geom_histogram(aes(y = ..count../sum(..count..)), binwidth=60*60,

scale_y_continuous(formatter="percent") +

messages.subject: Re: scale_x_datetime question
parts: Thank you guys. I figured it out. Problem was that a snippet from around the web used numeric limits which were generated via as.numeric from POSIXct values...
On Thu, Mar 24, 2011 at 5:49 AM, Kohske Takahashi <takahash...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi,

you need to specify the limits via POSIXct object:

ggplot(m, aes(x=as.POSIXct(format(m$date, "2000/01/01 %H:%M:%S")))) +
 geom_histogram(aes(y = ..count../sum(..count..)), binwidth=60*60,
colour="white", right=F) +
 scale_y_continuous(formatter="percent") +

scale_x_datetime(major="3 hours", format="%H:%M:%S",
limits=as.POSIXct(c("2000/01/01 02:00:00", "2000/01/01 21:00:00")))

note that 2000/01/01 is arbitral.

--
